# Finding out where things stand

All of these only read. Check each command's help, and prefer its JSON output.

| Question | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Which packages are there? | `vmono ls` |
| Which repositories does vmono know? | `vmono repos` |
| What is a package for, and what is in it? | `vmono show` |
| What work is there on a package? | `vmono session ls` |
| Where does one session stand, member by member? | `vmono status` |
| Where is it on disk? | `vmono path` |
| What would pushing it publish? | `vmono session review` |

Name the package, or the session as `package/session`: outside a session vmono
has little to infer them from.

What vmono says about remote branches and merges is as of the last fetch. Say so
when it matters.

Summarize for the user rather than pasting output: which sessions are in
progress, pushed or merged, any uncommitted work, and anything that needs them.
A merged session is usually done with: they can remove it, and more work belongs
in a new one.

To answer "is there already a package for this?", compare the members and
purposes of the packages with what the user wants to work on.
